verdicts.title: test_mode_switch_does_not_double_correct promises a reference comparison it never performs (the #405 vacuity pattern in a sibling file)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced by mutation. packages/opaque-optimizers/tests/test_adadelta.py:306-338: the docstring and the inline comment at :331-335 promise the post-switch update will 'match what we'd get with phi forced to zero (no double correction)', but the only post-switch assertion is 'assert torch.isfinite(updates_after[k]).all()' at :338 -- no phi-zero reference is computed and no comparison is made. I removed both 'and noisy_squared_grads is None' conditions from packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_adadelta.py (the phi_g guard at ~:236 and the phi_dx guard at ~:251), i.e. re-introduced exactly the double correction the test names as its regression target. 'uv run pytest packages/opaque-optimizers/tests/test_adadelta.py -k mode_switch' passed, and the entire optimizers suite (231 tests) passed with the mutation in place. The where-fallback (torch.where(corrected>0, corrected, v)) plus the clamp(min=0.0) and the additive eps in _rms keep the result finite under the mutation, so the finiteness assertion can never fail here. Source file restored to HEAD afterwards (git status clean). Issue #405 ('Replace vacuous optimizer regressions with behavior-sensitive tests') is CLOSED and its fix commit b9faed0a touched only _adagrad.py, _bias_correction.py, test_adagrad.py, test_rmsprop.py and test_state_dict.py -- test_adadelta.py was never touched, so this is a residual of a closed issue, not a duplicate of an open one. Low severity: test-quality gap only, no runtime defect today.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A refactor drops the 'and noisy_squared_grads is None' condition from the phi_g/phi_dx correction guards in _adadelta.py, so a SecondMomentNoiseOutput step subtracts the stale phi EMAs from the already-post-processing-debiased v_g/v_dx and skews the update magnitude. Verified by mutation: the dedicated regression test test_mode_switch_does_not_double_correct still passes, and so does the whole 231-test opaque-optimizers suite. The regression is caught nowhere.

verdicts.title: Dead bc_floor parameter left in Adadelta after the same cleanup removed it from Adagrad
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by reading and grep. packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_adadelta.py:121 declares 'bc_floor: float,' in _scale_by_adadelta's signature; :377 computes 'bc_floor = eps * eps' and :382 passes it. A grep for bc_floor across the whole file returns exactly those three hits -- the scaler body never reads it. The private second-moment branch instead guards with 'v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)' (a min=0 clamp, not an eps^2 floor), relying on the additive eps inside _rms for denominator safety. By contrast _rmsprop.py:124 and _adam.py:193 genuinely apply '.clamp(min=bc_floor)' in their noisy_squared_grads branches, and _adagrad.py has no bc_floor at all after b9faed0a. So the parameter is dead plumbing in Adadelta. The secondary claim about _bias_correction.py:31-34 is weaker than stated: that text reads 'The separate bc_floor clamp seen in some optimizers belongs to the private second-moment branch' -- hedged with 'some optimizers', so it is not literally false, only unhelpful next to Adadelta's live bc_floor plumbing. #405 (the cleanup issue) is closed; no open issue covers this.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Purely a maintenance/readability defect, no runtime behavior change. A maintainer auditing Adadelta's noisy_squared_grads branch sees adadelta() compute bc_floor = eps*eps and pass it into _scale_by_adadelta, and assumes an eps^2 denominator floor is applied there as it is in RMSprop (_rmsprop.py:124) and Adam (_adam.py:193). It is not: the branch clamps at min=0.0 and relies solely on the additive eps in _rms, a different numerical behavior from what the plumbing advertises.

verdicts.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token alignment term (and thus disagrees with TRL)
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified. (1) Implementation: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_wpo.py:63-67 computes avg_logp = sum(masked per_token_logps)/token_count and returns avg_logp.detach().exp() -- it takes no logits and applies no alignment term. (2) Paper: I fetched the arXiv HTML of 2406.11827 and the adopted 'sampled alignment' weight (Eq. 2) is w(x,y) = exp( (1/|y|) sum_t log [ pi(y_t|x,y_<t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v|x,y_<t)^2 ] ), and the paper states 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO due to its superior performance.' So the sum_v p_v^2 denominator IS part of the adopted formula. (3) Reference impl: trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 (installed at .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/trl) computes lse2 - 2*lse1 = log(sum_v p_v^2), subtracts it from per_token_logps, then averages and exponentiates -- with the comment 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper'. (4) Call site: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 multiplies the per-example loss by _wpo_weight(chosen)*_wpo_weight(rejected), and _wpo_weight (:1251-1267) already receives the full logits tensor, so the missing term is computable there without new plumbing. (5) The repo knows: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518-526 is a strict xfail naming exactly this omission; I ran it and it xfails as documented. Documentation claims the paper: _wpo.py's module docstring cites arXiv:2406.11827 and docs/reference/alignment.md:70 lists 'wpo_weights() -- per-example WPO weight (arXiv:2406.11827)'. Not tracked: both plausible umbrellas, #323 and #475, are CLOSED (2026-08-27), and a targeted issue search for WPO/use_weighting returned nothing. Severity medium, not high: use_weighting is opt-in, the deviation is a per-example reweighting of the loss with no privacy consequence (the weight is detached and per-example, so per-record sensitivity is unchanged), and the divergence is already pinned by a strict xfail -- but it is a silent, undocumented-to-users departure from the cited objective.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets DPOConfig(use_weighting=True) expecting the published WPO objective (and TRL-equivalent behavior). opaque's weight is exp(mean_t log p(y_t)); the paper's Eq. 2 and TRL both use exp(mean_t [log p(y_t) - log sum_v p(v)^2]). Since log sum_v p(v)^2 lies in [-log|V|, 0] and varies per token and per example, the two weights differ by a per-example factor exp(-mean_t log sum_v p_v^2) > 1 that is not constant across the batch, so relative pair weighting -- and hence training dynamics and results -- differ systematically from the cited method. No error, no warning; only a strict xfail in test_trl_parity.py records the gap.

verdicts.title: Docs still advertise the deleted SquareChiPO head as implemented
verdicts.reasoning: Verified. 'grep -rni squarechipo packages/ --include=*.py' returns nothing -- the head does not exist, and _DPO_HEADS in packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:81-98 has no 'squarechipo' entry (nor is it in _SPECIAL_CASED_HEADS at :110), so construction fails eagerly at :352-355 with a KeyError, i.e. fail-loud. Three doc sites still list it: docs/alignment/trainers.md:18 under 'The supported loss_type values map onto the corresponding alignment papers'; docs/alignment/dpo.md:46 under 'Implemented preference heads in this guide follow the primary papers for'; docs/reference/alignment.md:78 in the 'Primary papers for the implemented alignment objectives' list. Provenance confirmed and slightly different from the report's framing: 17c58f8c ('delete(alignment): remove non-private SquareChiPO (#502)') DID clean all three docs files; the citation-repair commit 1d216fcd ('docs(references): repair scholarly citations (#503)', merged 3 hours later) re-introduced the entries -- git log -S SquareChiPO on trainers.md shows 1d216fcd as the most recent touch. Mitigating: the authoritative supported-names table at docs/alignment/trainers.md:~209 correctly no longer lists squarechipo, so the drift is in the prose lists only. The umbrella docs issue #324 is CLOSED, so this is untracked. Low severity: docs-only, fail-loud on use.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads docs/alignment/trainers.md:18 ('the supported loss_type values ... SquareChiPO'), docs/alignment/dpo.md:46 ('Implemented preference heads'), or docs/reference/alignment.md:78 ('implemented alignment objectives') and concludes the DP SquareChiPO head ships. Setting loss_type='squarechipo' raises KeyError at DPOTrainer construction (_dpo_trainer.py:352-355) -- fail-loud, no silent wrong training. The cost is wasted planning around a privacy-relevant capability the library does not have; the supported-names table further down the same page contradicts the prose.

verdicts.title: Chat-template transform: overstated coverage comments and exact-string generation-marker guards
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced all three sub-claims against real templates downloaded from the Hub. (a) Running get_training_chat_template on the real Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct template (NousResearch mirror), the real gemma-3-1b-it template (unsloth mirror), and the canonical shared-expression ChatML template all raise ValueError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'); gemma-2-2b-it and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct succeed. So the Strategy-2 comment 'Handles ChatML, Llama-3, Phi-3, etc.' (_chat_template.py:229) and the _wrap_gemma_shared_expression docstring 'Gemma 2/3 templates' (:376-380) overstate coverage. The Gemma-3 mechanism is exactly as reported: content_pat = re.compile(r"\{\{-?\s*[^}]*\bcontent\b[^}]*-?\}\}") finds 2 matches in the real Gemma-3 template -- "{{ message['content'] | trim }}" and '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' -- so the len(content_matches) != 1 check at :403-406 returns None. (b) The idempotency check at :214 is 'if _GEN_START in template' with _GEN_START == '{% generation %}' exactly; feeding a template that already carries '{%- generation -%}' / '{%- endgeneration -%}' produced a nested '{%- generation -%}{% generation %}...{% endgeneration %}{%- endgeneration -%}' wrapper rather than returning unchanged. transformers 5.x accepts whitespace-control variants (chat_template_utils.py:508 uses re.search(r"\{\%-?\s*generation\s*-?\%\}")), and _completion_mask.py:84 uses the same exact-substring test, so a validly pre-marked template is rejected there. Everything here is fail-closed or benign-redundant: no wrong assistant mask is produced in any of the paths I exercised. No open issue matches (targeted search returned nothing; the related #387 work is not in the open snapshot). Low severity is right.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Two confusing-but-safe outcomes, both reproduced. (1) Completion-only-loss chat data with a real Llama-3-Instruct, real Gemma-3, or canonical shared-expression ChatML tokenizer: get_training_chat_template raises ValueError at dataset prep, despite the source comment claiming ChatML/Llama-3 support and the Gemma helper claiming Gemma 2/3 (Gemma-3 fails specifically because its raise_exception expression is a second \bcontent\b match, tripping the len != 1 bail at _chat_template.py:405). (2) A user who hand-installed the whitespace-control markers '{%- generation -%}' (valid per transformers' regex) gets get_training_chat_template producing a redundant nested marker pair, and apply_chat_template_with_mask (_completion_mask.py:84) rejecting the template with a message telling them to install markers they already have. No incorrect mask is ever produced -- the nesting yields duplicated identical spans.

verdicts.title: DiscoPOP module cites a fabricated author/title; sequence_logp docstring denies the ld_alpha feature it implements
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified by reading the files. (a) packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_discopop.py:5-7 attributes the method to 'Azar, M. G., et al. (2024). DiscoPOP: Discovering Preference Optimization Procedures Using Self-Supervised Feedback. NeurIPS 2024.', and discopop_loss's own docstring (:41) repeats '(Azar 2024 / NeurIPS 2024)'. That author+title combination does not exist: DiscoPOP is Lu et al., 'Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models' (arXiv:2406.08414), which docs/reference/alignment.md:72 cites correctly, while Azar et al. is the IPO paper (cited correctly two lines above at :70 for ipo_loss). The citation-repair commit 1d216fcd (#503) touched only docs/, never packages/, so the source-level misattribution survived. (b) The path in the report is slightly wrong -- the file is packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/logprob/_sequence.py, not .../alignment/dpo/logprob/_sequence.py -- but the content claim is exact: the module docstring at :15-16 says 'The ld_alpha (LD-DPO, arXiv:2409.06411) length-desensitised logp split is not implemented here; pass ld_alpha=None', while sequence_logp in the same file takes ld_alpha (:36), documents it (:53-61, :71), and implements the prefix/tail split at :81-96. The real limitation is scoped correctly on fused_sequence_logp's own docstring (:133-134: 'The LD-DPO ld_alpha split is not supported on the fused path'), which is what the module docstring over-generalizes. This is documentation-only; both functions behave correctly. The docs umbrella #324 is closed, so untracked. Low severity, and note the project's own DP review protocol explicitly forbids invented citations, which is what makes (a) worth fixing despite being prose.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Documentation-only, no runtime defect. (a) A reviewer or user following _discopop.py's in-source reference searches for a DiscoPOP paper by Azar et al. with the subtitle 'Using Self-Supervised Feedback' and finds nothing, or lands on Azar et al.'s IPO paper and tries to verify the logistic/exponential gate formula against the wrong objective; the repo's own docs/reference/alignment.md:72 already carries the correct Lu et al. / arXiv:2406.08414 citation. (b) A caller reading the module docstring of packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/logprob/_sequence.py concludes ld_alpha is unimplemented and builds a manual LD-DPO split, even though sequence_logp implements it at :81-96; only fused_sequence_logp actually lacks it.
